newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares firm, calmer after political jitters.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares firm, calmer after political jitters.

text.p: OSLO, shares advanced on Thursday recapturing most of day-earlier losses when a jittery market fell after Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland announced her resignation. Brokers said the downward move was exaggerated and that sentiment was positive.
"The market is back on track after the volatility yesterday which was mainly a misunderstanding by foreigners who thought there would be a snap general election," said one broker.
"Generally sentiment is good with investors believing in good economic growth. Norway seems a very attractive place to have your money invested."
The Total share index climed 0.78 percent to 876.33 points in turnover of 749 million crowns.

Hydro accounted for more than six percent of trade and gained one crown to close at 299 crowns. Brokers said buying interest had picked up following the fall in price since the group released nine-month results on Monday.

Trade was also brisk in Petroleum Geo-Services which gained strongly on higher than expected third-quarter earnings. PGS peaked at 236 crowns before falling back to close at 224 crowns, a gain of 11.50 crowns.
